content:
Congrats on the launch! While the agents are grinding through the first PR https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/pull/1039, I am wondering how to get more roadmaps added and after reading the README, I still have some questions unanswered. I want to check alignment because roadmaps are human reviewed AFAICT and don't want to waste human time:

  • is there more guidance of what content belongs in TauCeti? Is "there is a Springer GTM book on that theory/results" a good proxy for something that would be desirable?
  • also is there any rough sizing on how large/small would a should a roadmap project be? Roughly one math textbook of content? Maybe of the order of 10k-100k loc of lean code? Some other measure?
  • do you have some set of expectations from the roadmap human proposer? Obviously the extremes - zero human knowledge, pure AI roadmap (don't bother sending) and world-class expert in the are (absolutely please send) are clear, but how about "I have a vague understanding of the topic and AI cowrote the roadmap", or "I took a grad level class on it many years ago, and AI helped me write the roadmap", etc?
  • are there plans already underway to expand the list of roadmaps (like lean-eval with Oliver Knill's 'Some Fundamental Theorems in Mathematics')? Or you prefer to get more of the existing roadmaps done before scaling up? Maybe one roadmap per major area of math?
(Contained in) a Springer GTM definitely sounds good.

Yes, if there is a GTM about it is is certainly in scope. If you can plausibly imagine a conference, where are significant fraction of the attendees would self-identify as mathematicians, and it would be reasonable to expect that graduate students there knew about a particular result, then it's in scope.

Re size: I think 10k LOC is a reasonable lower bound, but 100k might be better. In terms of books/articles, I think 1-10 research papers is reasonable, and 1-2 books is good.

(My TauCetiRoadmap#62 draft roadmap on representation theory is probably too big, attempting to distill down from about 10 graduate level representation theory textbooks.)
Re: expertise required. I think "I took a grad level class years ago, and AI helped me write" is fine, but "vague understanding and AI wrote most" is not.

There are no particular plans to systematically expand the roadmap list: I want this to happen organically by participants here deciding to write them. (An item high on my TODO list is inviting/encouraging particular people to write roadmaps: please consider yourself invited to write roadmaps, and even better to go out and encourage subject area experts to write them --- I don't think any Lean knowledge is actually required.)

Re: the balance of more roadmaps vs more content PRs... I don't know yet. Let's see how many tokens people start pouring into making content PRs and/or just running ./tauceti work --loop. We are just going to need to calibrate to keep these in balance. Maybe we should aim that "open roadmaps < 100 * completed roadmaps", for some value of 100. Very open to discussion here!
(Thank you for these questions, after we've had a chance to discussion my tentative answers here, I'll roll the conclusions back into the documentation.)

I don't think any Lean knowledge is actually required

Then what is expected of a roadmap? How is it different from a textbook or several papers?
Have you looked at one? It looks nothing like a textbook, it's much briefer.
